placements.quote: Its first phase, LEGEND-200, reuses the GERDA cryostat in Hall A of the Laboratori Nazionali del Gran Sasso (LNGS) underground laboratory in Italy

isotope.quote: searches for the 0νββ of 76Ge using High Purity Germanium detectors enriched in 76Ge beyond the 86%

isotope_mass.quote: LEGEND-200, operating up to 200 kg of enriched germanium detectors immersed in liquid argon at the INFN Gran Sasso National Laboratory (LNGS), represents the first stage of the LEGEND scientific program.

enrichment.quote: High Purity Germanium detectors enriched in 76Ge beyond the 86%

summary.plain: Up to 200 kilograms of enriched germanium detectors immersed in liquid argon in the same Italian underground hall used by the earlier GERDA experiment, watching for a rare radioactive decay.
summary.technical: LEGEND-200: up to 200 kg of enriched (>86% 76Ge) HPGe detectors immersed in a liquid-argon active shield at LNGS, reusing the GERDA cryostat infrastructure; taking data since 2023.

technology.locator: LEGEND-200 first-results paper (arXiv:2509.21166), detector description; LEGEND official site
technology.quote: The HPGe detectors array is the core of the LEGEND-200 experiment, represented in Fig. 3. These detectors are operated bare in a 64 m3 Liquid Argon (LAr) cryostat at ∼ 88 K. LAr serves not only as a coolant and as a passive shield, but also as an active background veto
technology.value: Enriched high-purity germanium detectors immersed in a liquid-argon active shield
